item.title: Yangian for $\mathfrak{gl}_{2}$ and Gelfand-Tsetlin basis for $\mathfrak{gl}_{n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an explicit realization of finite-dimensional irreducible representations $V_{\lambda}$ of $\mathfrak{gl}_{n}$ using the representation theory of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})$. We consider $V_{\lambda}$ as the evaluation representation of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n})$ and restrict it to the subalgebras $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})^{(i)}$. Then $V_{\lambda}$ is completely reducible as a representation of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})^{(i)}$. It allows us to use the explicit formulas for irreducible representations of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})$.
item.dc:creator: Mark Belov

item.title: Polytopal invariance for Lusztig's $q$-weight multiplicities
item.description: arXiv:2610.14275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Phi$ be an irreducible root system normalized so that long roots have length $\sqrt{2}$, and let $\mu\leq\lambda$ be dominant weights. We associate to $(\Phi,\mu,\lambda)$ the convex polytope $$P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda} = (\mu+C)\cap(\lambda-C)\cap(\overline{D}-\rho),$$ where $C=\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\Phi^+$ and $\overline{D}$ is the closed dominant Weyl chamber. We prove that if $P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda}$ and $P^{\Phi'}_{\mu',\lambda'}$ are isometric, then $$K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)=K^{\Phi'}_{\lambda'\mu'}(q),$$ where $K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)$ is Lusztig's $q$-analogue of the $\mu$-weight multiplicity in the irreducible highest-weight representation $V(\lambda)$, often called the generalized Kostka-Foulkes polynomial. Moreover, we construct the polynomial directly from the metric shape of the polytope, and we classify when two such polytopes are isometric. Such coincidences are abundant and can occur in different Dynkin types, and in different Dynkin families. By the Lusztig-Kato theorem, the main theorem gives a metric analogue, in the spherical setting, of the combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\'as Libedinsky

item.title: Multiplicity One and van Dijk's Conjecture for Connected Complex Symmetric Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.14540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give new invariant-theoretic proofs of regularity for the three classical residual families DIII, balanced CII, and BDI/Spin. In DIII and balanced CII, trace contractions and a supertrace identity show that the relevant character spaces in the quadratic moment quotient vanish. These quotient-level vanishings lift to the corresponding equivariant tempered-distribution vanishings. In BDI/Spin, Gram matrices and a volume tensor give the analogous vanishing for the two single-determinant characters. We also give a direct proof of the required equivariant-distribution vanishing for EVII. These results, together with corrected distinguished-nilpotent calculations for the nice factors, establish the required componentwise regularity for the finite-component data attached to all irreducible factors and repair gaps in the previously proposed proofs. Combining these factorwise results across products and finite central quotients yields regularity for every symmetric pair of a connected complex reductive group. Generalized Harish-Chandra descent and a compatible Chevalley involution give multiplicity one for irreducible Casselman-Wallach representations in the connected-group case. A finite-component restriction argument extends this multiplicity-one statement to every possibly disconnected complex reductive $G$ whose symmetric space $G/G^\theta$ is connected. Consequently, we establish van Dijk's conjecture on the unitary Gelfand property for connected complex symmetric spaces.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Ge

item.title: The Cartan determinant conjecture for representation-finite algebras over perfect fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.14638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field and let $A$ be a finite-dimensional representation-finite $k$-algebra. We prove that finite global dimension implies that the integral Cartan determinant of $A$ is one, extending Enomoto's result from algebraically closed fields to perfect fields.
item.dc:creator: Liang Chen

item.title: A Counterexample To The TF-cone Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.14814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The TF-cone conjecture of Asai and Iyama predicts that the TF equivalence class of an integral $g$-vector is the open cone generated by the canonical summands of all its positive multiples. We give a counterexample to this conjecture. For the tensor product of the three-arrow Kronecker algebra with the path algebra of $s\to t$, a vector $w$ has a two-dimensional TF equivalence class, whereas every positive integral multiple $mw$ is generically indecomposable. The cone generated by these canonical summands is therefore a single ray. The same example disproves the relative-interior version proposed by Haerizadeh and Yassemi.
item.dc:creator: Jindong Yan, Shenglin Zhu

item.title: Differential operator approach to the $\imath$Howe duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.14872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The iHowe duality for iquantum groups of type AIII/IV was established in \cite{LX22} via two approaches, based on partial flag varieties and quantum coordinate coalgebras respectively. In this paper, we provide a new construction of this iHowe duality via quantum differential operators. Moreover, by deriving explicit action formulas, we prove that our construction coincides with the two constructions given in \cite{LX22}.
item.dc:creator: Qianqi Wang

item.title: Ideal filtrations and stabilization in alternating HRS tilting
item.description: arXiv:2610.14914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the realization functors obtained by alternating forward and backward HRS tilts of any torsion pair over a finite-dimensional algebra are equivalences from some step onward. The number of steps is bounded by the lengths of the indecomposable projective modules. The even hearts define an increasing filtration of ideals contained in a square-zero ideal. For a torsion pair induced by a two-term silting complex, we identify the successive layers with Buan-Zhou kernel ideals and compute them by reduction modulo the successive ideals. We also describe the largest quotient over which the complex becomes tilting and determine the exact stabilization index from the two parity heights. We construct algebras for which the HRS height is arbitrarily large, and compute their ideal filtrations.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Han, Ping He

item.title: Tate cohomology of unipotent cuspidal representations of finite groups of Lie type
item.description: arXiv:2610.15037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $k$ be an algebraic closure of the finite field with $p$ elements. Let $G$ be a connected reductive algebraic group over $k$, and let $F:G\rightarrow G$ be a Frobenius morphism, defining an $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational structure on $G$, where $q$ is a power of $p$. Let $\ell$ be a prime different from $p$ and $\ell\ne 2$. Let $\Pi$ be an $\ell$-adic cuspidal unipotent representation of $G^{F^\ell}$ such that $\Pi\simeq \Pi^\sigma$, where $\sigma$ is a generator the Galois group ${\rm Gal}(\mathbb{F}_{q^\ell}/\mathbb{F}_q)$. In this paper, we prove the irreducibility of the zeroth Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^0(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ and vanishing of the first Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^1(\sigma,\mathcal{L})$ for any $G^{F^\ell}\rtimes{\rm Gal}(\mathbb{F}_{q^\ell}/\mathbb{F}_q)$-stable lattice $\mathcal{L}$ in $\Pi$, using the multiplicity-one property of a progenerator constructed via the generalized Gelfand-Graev representations and Harish-Chandra induction.
item.dc:creator: Sabyasachi Dhar

item.title: Unipotent quotients in compactified Coxeter varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.15278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we extend Lusztig's description of quotients of Coxeter varieties by unipotent radicals of parabolic subgroups, to quotients of certain open neighbourhoods in the smooth compactification of Coxeter varieties. These quotients are products of an affine space with a Coxeter variety for an associated Levi quotient, and this result holds uniformly for any connected reductive group over a finite field. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Wang computing the invariants, under the action of unipotent subgroups, of the cohomology of the Deligne-Lusztig coverings of Coxeter varieties. We also prove that derived Alvis-Curtis duality sends the compactly supported cohomology of these coverings to their ordinary cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Muller

item.title: A trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $\mathrm{GL}_{n}(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n}(E)$, with $E/F$ a quadratic extension of non-Archimedean local fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.15432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the classical trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $p$-adic reductive groups, given by Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan in 1986, to a relative case. That is when $E/F$ is a quadratic extension of $p$-adic fields, the main result is a scalar Paley-Wiener theorem for relative Bessel distributions on $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$. These distributions are relative character of the form $$\pi\mapsto I_\pi (f), \ f\in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(E)),$$ as $\pi$ ranges over $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-distinguished irreducible tempered representations, and are constructed from a $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-invariant functional and a Whittaker functional. Using the local Langlands correspondence, and the base-change from a unitary group, we show that the relative characters can be described as elements of the "generic" Bernstein center of the unitary group $U(n)$.
item.dc:creator: Juliette Coutens

item.title: On a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type
item.description: arXiv:2610.15517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a family $(\Lambda_\lambda)_{\lambda \in \Bbbk^\times}$ of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type over an algebraically closed field $\Bbbk$, where $\Bbbk^\times:= \Bbbk\setminus \{0\}$, and for each $\lambda \in \Bbbk^\times$, $\Lambda_\lambda$ is socle equivalent to $\Lambda_1$, which is the trivial extension of a hereditary algebra of type $\tilde{A}$. We compute their Hochschild cohomologies, which shows that $\Lambda_\lambda$ is not derived equivalent to $\Lambda_1$ if $\lambda \neq 1$. This means that a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type given by Bocian--Holm--Skowro{\' n}ski is not complete.
item.dc:creator: Hideto Asashiba, Ayako Itaba, Manuel Saorin

item.title: Parabolically induced representations of $GL_n(O_l)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.15762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be the ring of integers of a non-Archimedean local field with uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $\mathcal O_\ell=\mathcal O/\varpi^\ell\mathcal O$ for $\ell\geq1$. In this article, we study representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_\ell)$ parabolically induced from characters of the Borel subgroup $\mathrm{B}_n(\mathcal O_\ell)$. For $n=3$, we establish a criterion for the irreducibility of these induced representations in terms of the relative conductors of the inducing characters. Motivated by this result, we formulate a conjecture characterizing the irreducibility of such representations for arbitrary $n$. We further show that when all inducing characters are equal, the resulting induced representation is not multiplicity-free, implying that the corresponding triple $(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_\ell),\mathrm{B}_n(\mathcal O_\ell),\chi)$ is not a Gelfand pair. Finally, we study the irreducible decomposition of these representations for $\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathcal O_\ell)$ when two relative conductors attain their maximal values. Using the decomposition theory for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal O_\ell)$, we describe the irreducible constituents and determine their dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Prem Dagar

item.title: Finite Length of Locally Analytic Vectors for $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and $D_F^\times$
item.description: arXiv:2610.15841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F/\mathbf Q_p$ and $E/\mathbf Q_p$ be finite extensions, and let $G=\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ or $D_F^\times$, where $D_F$ is the quaternion division algebra over $F$. Let $\Pi$ be an admissible Banach $E$-representation of $G$ whose locally $\mathbf Q_p$-analytic vectors $\Pi^{\mathrm{an}}$ have an infinitesimal character. If $p>2$ or $F=\mathbf Q_p$, we prove that $\Pi^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $\Pi$ have finite length in their respective admissible categories.
item.dc:creator: Pengcheng Ding

item.title: Finite Root Sums in Symmetrizable Kac-Moody Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.15923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra with root system $\Phi$. A subset $S\subseteq\Phi$ is \emph{closed} if $\alpha,\beta\in S$ and $\alpha+\beta\in\Phi$ imply $\alpha+\beta\in S$. For finite and affine Kac-Moody algebras, this closure property is known to extend from pairs to arbitrary finite sums that are roots. We prove that every closed subset of the root system of any symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra is closed under arbitrary finite sums that are roots. The proof uses real-root strings and simultaneous separation of positive imaginary roots, together with an addition lemma for fundamental imaginary roots. As an application, we extend a necessary condition for wideness of regular subalgebras from finite and affine types to all symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebras: the symmetric closure of the roots associated to a wide regular subalgebra is the entire root system.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Douglas

item.title: Representation Type and Schurian Finiteness of Tits Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.16214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the representation type and Schurian finiteness of the Tits algebra of a finite central real hyperplane arrangement over an algebraically closed field. The algebra is representation-finite when the arrangement has at most two hyperplanes, tame when it has three, and wild when it has at least four. Moreover, it is Schurian-finite if and only if the arrangement has at most two hyperplanes. Both classifications hold over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. The proof combines Saliola's bound-quiver presentation with explicit module constructions, convex subquivers, essentialization, and deletion. In the $\mathbb{R}^2$ case, we describe all eleven indecomposable modules for two lines and construct a full exact embedding of modules over a free algebra for at least four lines.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Chen

item.title: Regularity of Totally Nonnegative Wonderful Compactification
item.description: arXiv:2610.16332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a split real semisimple group of adjoint type. We prove that the cellular decomposition of the totally nonnegative part of its wonderful compactification is a regular CW complex, confirming a conjecture of Galashin, Karp, and Lam. In particular, the closure of every cell is homeomorphic to a closed ball. The proof combines a Bruhat atlas compatible with total positivity and a CL-labeling of the augmented face poset. The atlas models the strata locally with open Richardson varieties in the flag variety of a larger Kac-Moody group and identifies their totally nonnegative cells.
item.dc:creator: Xuhua He, Kaitao Xie

item.title: Double Bruhat cells in symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the closures of the double Bruhat cells of symmetric spacess in its equivariant embeddings. We call them large double Bruhat varieties. Our aim is to establish the double Bruhat stratification as a natural setting for extending the geometry of Richardson varieties to symmetric spaces. For the wonderful compactification of the associated adjoint symmetric space, we show their scheme-theoretic intersections with the unique closed orbit are reduced unions of projected Richardson varieties. This connection with Richardson geometry on partial flag varieties supports large double Bruhat varieties as a natural class of subvarieties in symmetric-space embeddings. In positive characteristic, we prove that every equivariant embedding admits a Frobenius splitting compatible with all large double Bruhat varieties and all boundary divisors. These varieties are strongly F-regular, and globally F-regular when the ambient embedding is projective. In characteristic zero, they are of strongly F-regular type, and of globally F-regular type in the projective case; in particular, they are normal, Cohen-Macaulay, and have rational singularities.
item.dc:creator: Huanchen Bao, Jinfeng Song

item.title: Ideal quotients of $n$-exact categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.16403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we extend the notion of a removable subcategory to $n$-exact categories, and prove that an ideal quotient by a subcategory of projective-injectives inherits an $n$-exact structure from the original category if and only if the subcategory is removable. In the Frobenius case, the quotient remains Frobenius, and the stable $(n+2)$-angulated categories are equivalent. We give a sufficient condition for a subcategory of projective-injectives to be removable. We also show that the ideal quotient construction is compatible with cluster tilting. Finally, we apply the construction to $2$-cluster tilting subcategories of the category of ACM bundles on a Geigle--Lenzing projective plane, obtaining quotients for both natural and relative $2$-exact structures.
item.dc:creator: Weikang Weng

item.title: Depth-zero local Langlands via shtukas in mixed characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.16445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assuming a smoothness property for mixed-characteristic shtuka spaces and hyperbolic localization for twisted sheaves, we determine the inertial restriction of the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter for irreducible depth-zero representations. Let $E$ be a non-archimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$, let $G$ be an unramified connected reductive group over $E$, and let $\pi$ be an irreducible smooth depth-zero representation of $G(E)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{\ell}$ where $\ell$ is a prime number which does not divide $p|\pi_0Z(G)|$. Let $\varphi_{\pi}^{\operatorname{FS}}$ be the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter associated to $\pi$. We describe the restriction of $\varphi_{\pi}^{\operatorname{FS}}$ to the inertia subgroup in terms of Deligne-Lusztig theory. We prove this by computing the inertia action on the cohomology of shtuka spaces with depth-zero level structure. As an application, we prove that the Fargues--Scholze $L$-parameters agree with DeBacker--Reeder $L$-parameters over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\ell}$.
item.dc:creator: Chenji Fu

item.title: The modulo distinction problem for D*
item.description: arXiv:2610.16877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero and residue characteristic $p$. Let $E$ be a quadratic field extension of $F$. Let $D$ be the unique quaternion division algebra defined over $F$. Let $G=\GL_{2}(E)$ and $H=D^\times$. This paper studies the modulo distinction problem for the pair $(G,H)$ with $\ell\neq p$, which gives a complete classification of $H$-distinguished representations of $G$, including the cases $\ell=2$ and $p=2$. In terms of type theory, we give a complete classification of $H$-distinguished supercuspidal representations when $p$ is odd.
item.dc:creator: Junyan Liu, Hengfei Lu

item.title: Microlocal Arthur packets as a quasi-canonical basis of stable distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that microlocal Arthur packets can be reconstructed from an otherwise underdetermined system of linear equations arising from Kashiwara's local index theorem. The key is a geometric rigidity property of Arthur orbits which, together with Fourier symmetry, uniquely determines the microlocal multiplicities defining these packets. This realizes the associated Arthur distribution as the unique normalized element in the intersection of two filtered spaces of standard stable distributions related by Fourier transform. Under standard enhanced local Langlands hypotheses and Aubert compatibility, this gives an alternative representation-theoretic definition of microlocal Arthur packets for general connected reductive $p$-adic groups that does not use twisted endoscopy and ensures stability through the stability of tempered packet distributions. In the unipotent setting, we use this characterization to prove agreement between endoscopic and microlocal Arthur packets for split $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ when the residue characteristic is at least $6n+4$. We further use this characterization to compute all unipotent Arthur packets with unramified real infinitesimal character for inner-to-split adjoint exceptional $p$-adic groups. In this exceptional setting, we prove the microlocal weak Arthur packet conjecture and give counterexamples to the microlocal analogues of the least- and greatest-parameter conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Dan Ciubotaru, Emile Okada

item.title: $E$-symmetric algebras I
item.description: arXiv:2610.17070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study various symmetry conditions related to the Auslander-Reiten formula for finite-dimensional algebras. In particular, we define a new class of algebras which we call $E$-symmetric. A theorem by Derksen-Weyman-Zelevinksy implies that all Jacobian algebras are $E$-symmetric. We prove the converse for the class of monomial algebras.
item.dc:creator: Grzegorz Bobi\'nski, Jan Schr\"oer

item.title: Square integrable representations and Hecke eigenvalues over a local non-archimedian field
item.description: arXiv:2610.17317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected semi-simple group over a local non-archimedean field $F$. In this paper we study the action of Hecke operators on the Schwartz space of half-densities on the moduli stack $\bpo$ of $G$-bundles on ${\mathbb P}^1$ endowed with a trivialization at $0$ and $\infty$. This space is a representation of $G(F)\times G(F)$ which contains the regular representation of $G(F)$. We show that this inclusion is an isomorphism on the cuspidal part. In addition we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation $\pi$ of $G(F)$ defines a Hecke eigenvalue. As a byproduct we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation of $G(F)$ with an Iwahori fixed vector defines a ${\mathbb C}$-point on the Calogero-Moser space associated to $G$. We also show that for $G=PGL(N)$ the eigenvalues of certain "simplest non-trivial" Hecke operators are essentially equal to the values of the character of $\pi$ on regular elliptic elements. These results are parallel to some of the results of our previous publication where some analogous statements are proved in the case when $F$ is a finite field.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Braverman, David Kazhdan

item.title: A subcategory with remarkable homological properties via actions of tensor categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.17646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By equipping the category $\mathcal{M}$ of modules over a finite dimensional algebra with the action of a finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$, we introduce a subcategory $\mathcal{PM}$ satisfying numerous remarkable properties: it is generating and cogenerating, functorially finite, closed under Auslander--Reiten translations (i.e. precluster tilting), and it computes the finitistic dimension. Through a functor category perspective, $\mathcal{PM}$ is identified with the $\mathcal{C}$-module functors that are projective, and we also prove a $\mathcal{C}$-equivariant version of the Auslander(--Solberg) correspondence. As examples, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ contains only finitely many indecomposable modules for some tensor product algebras. For some family of 1-Iwanaga--Gorenstein algebras introduced by Geiss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ is exactly the subcategory of $\tau$-locally free modules.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Coulembier, Edmund Heng

item.title: The algebraic theory of non-archimedean intertwining periods
item.description: arXiv:2610.17783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an algebraic theory of local intertwining periods for symmetric pairs $(G,H,\theta)$ over non-archimedean local fields $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and finite-length representations of Levi subgroups of $G$ with coefficients in an algebraically closed field $R$ of characteristic different from the residual characteristic of $F$. For open orbits this algebraic version is essentially contained in the work of Blanc and Delorme. The algebraic theory relies on a crucial new uniqueness result, extending a result of Blanc and Delorme for open periods, which asserts that an admissible intertwining period is the only $H$-equivariant linear form extending the corresponding integral on the space of well-supported sections. Moreover the algebraic construction does not require the unimodularity hypothesis imposed in the work of Matringe--Offen--Yang. When $R=\mathbb{C}$, we also remove this assumption in the classical non-archimedean analytic setting, and prove convergence of intertwining periods for all symmetric spaces. At the same time we extend the context of the whole theory in the following manner: we allow $F$ to be of positive odd characteristic, we allow twisting characters in the periods, and we allow $H$ to lie between $(\mathbb{G}^\theta)^\circ(F)$ and $G^\theta$. Finally, in the algebraic setting, as in the work of Blanc and Delorme on open periods, we obtain explicit bounding polynomials for the singularities of the intertwining period. Such bounds are a key ingredient of a new proof of the cuspidal case of a conjecture of D. Prasad on quaternionic symplectic models.
item.dc:creator: Fei Chen, Nadir Matringe

item.title: Multiplicity One for Five Strongly Tempered Spherical Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.17888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero. We prove multiplicity one for every irreducible smooth admissible representation in the split forms of Wan-Zhang Models 6-10. Combining the Gelfand-Kazhdan method with nilpotent-wavefront restrictions on Bernstein-finite equivariant distributions, we establish the required symmetries through rational orbit analysis, parabolic descent, stabilizer characters, and conormal arguments. The type-$D_6$ analysis treats both the vector-similitude group of Model 9 and the semispin form arising in the exceptional $E_7$ model. For Model 10, the distribution theorem gives a product bound for periods; the individual multiplicity bound follows from Langlands classification and a vanishing theorem for standard modules induced from nongeneric tempered data on the maximal $E_6$ Levi.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Ge

item.title: Automorphisms of medium algebras and quasi-anisotropic real affine Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2610.18170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study automorphisms of Hausel's medium algebras by identifying them with equivariant cohomology algebras of affine Schubert varieties of a complex reductive group $G$. The automorphisms in question are then given by the action of either complex automorphisms or real structures of $G$ on affine Schubert varieties. We focus on describing the fixed points of those automorphisms on the spectra of medium algebras, and prove that the torsion-free quotients of the corresponding coinvariant algebras are isomorphic to equivariant cohomology rings of fixed loci in affine Schubert varieties. In the case of real structures, this naturally leads to and involves the study of affine Grassmannians for quasi-anisotropic (also called quasi-compact) real reductive groups, closely related to recent work of O'Brien. We also discuss relations to automorphisms of Higgs bundle moduli and to symmetric pair variants of medium algebras.
item.dc:creator: Mischa Elkner

item.title: Minimal presentations of finite-dimensional representations of pseudocompact algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.18805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a general formula for minimal projective presentations and for minimal discrete-injective presentations of finite-dimensional modules over basic pseudocompact algebras. We also show that the representation-theoretic g-vector of a module coincides with its DWZ-g-vector. These results generalize the description that Derksen, Weyman and Zelevinsky gave of minimal projective presentations for modules over certain finite-dimensional Jacobian algebras. In particular, we can drop their finiteness assumption, and we may work over fields of arbitrary characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Christof Geiss, Carolin Hartung, Daniel Labardini-Fragoso, Jan Schr\"oer

item.title: Equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations on Hermitian symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.14045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate and solve a $G$-equivariant analogue of the Seiberg-Witten equations on any irreducible Hermitian symmetric space $G/K$. We use a canonical $K$-invariant form to define a twisted Hodge operator generalising self-duality to higher dimensions. The resulting equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations arise, for a compact $G/K$, as conditions for the absolute minima of an energy functional. Their linear part has a representation theoretic interpretation: the same Weyl group data control the highest-weight realisation of the positive Dirac kernel in the compact case and its discrete-series realisation on the non-compact dual. This space of harmonic spinors collapses almost entirely by the quadratic conditions of the monopole equation. In the compact case, the equivariant moduli set, when non-empty, is a single gauge class, identifying with the $G$-invariant part of Bradlow's trichotomy for vortices, while in the non-compact case, every irreducible solution sits outside the discrete series.
item.dc:creator: Rafailia-Persefoni Tsiavou

item.title: Representation homology of involutive algebras and hyperoctaherdral homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.14278v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the (involutive) representation homology of involutive algebras, following the development of representation homology of associative algebra in our earlier papers. Our main motivation is to understand the hyperoctahedral homology of involutive algebras. We show that over a field of characteristic $0$, the hyperoctahedral homology of an involutive algebra is isomorphic (as a graded commutative algebra) to its one dimensional involutive representation homology. This result enables the explicit computation of the hyperoctahedral homology of the universal enveloping algebras of involutive (DG) Lie algebras. For group algebras $k[\Gamma]$ equipped with the involution $g \mapsto g^{-1}$, we relate the involutive representation homology of $k[\Gamma]$ to the representation homology of the group $\Gamma$ with coefficients in $\mu_2$, and we show that the latter is the homology of the loop space of the mod $2$ Dold-Thom space of $B\Gamma$; more generally, we compute the representation homology of $\Gamma$ with coefficients in an arbitrary diagonalizable group scheme. As a consequence, the hyperoctahedral homology of $k[\Gamma]$ is concentrated in degree $0$ in characteristic $0$, for every $\Gamma$.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Berest, Ajay C. Ramadoss, John Wood

item.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
item.description: arXiv:2610.14467v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.
item.dc:creator: Ce Wang

item.title: Bounds for (k,c) model functions over p-adic fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.14744v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field, let $k,c\ge1$, and let $\rho$ be a $(k,c)$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_{kc}(F)$: a complex representation of finite length whose wave front set has $(k^c)$ as its unique maximal orbit, and which admits a $(k,c)$ functional that is unique up to scaling. We prove that the functions in the $(k,c)$ model of $\rho$ are of moderate growth, by relating this model to the Zelevinsky model of $\rho$, and obtain as a consequence a bound for the restriction of these functions to the standard Levi subgroup associated with the composition $(c^k)$ of $kc$. As applications, we study convergence problems of several integrals involving $(k,c)$ models: integrals from the generalized doubling method, and a new family of integrals which extends the Rankin--Selberg integrals for Speh representations of Lapid and Mao.
item.dc:creator: Eyal Kaplan

item.title: Clifford Invariants and Three-Copy Quantum Tests
item.description: arXiv:2610.14758v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an explicit treatment of the third tensor power of the Clifford representation on $n$ qutrits, for $n\geq2$. This representation has five pairwise inequivalent irreducible constituents, with multiplicities $1,1,1,1,2$. The decomposition reduces the Clifford twirl of a tensor cube to four real parameters. Two of them are spectral moments of the input. The other two are cubic invariants expressed as sums of cubes of the Weyl characteristic function and the discrete Wigner function. On trace-one Hermitian matrices, the invariant polynomials of degree at most three are spanned by the constant function and four algebraically independent functions. These functions do not separate Clifford orbits. For pure inputs a single parameter suffices. We recover its range and the characterization of its maximum by stabilizer states. We bound the stabilizer fidelity, determine full separability across the three copies in the symmetric family, and recover the criterion for a complex projective $3$-design. We classify the jointly invariant quantum Boolean functions. For stabilizer testing and for testing unknown observables we give explicit bounds on copies and queries. We also give character formulas for the finite projective Clifford groups and record the complete character table for two qutrits.
item.dc:creator: Xingya Fan, Yongzhi Luan

item.title: Affine realization of tilted Richardson varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.14991v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Richardson varieties provide geometric representatives for products of Schubert classes, with stratifications indexed by the subintervals of Bruhat intervals. We construct analogous geometric models for tilted Bruhat intervals for all split connected reductive groups. Our construction uses Richardson varieties in affine flag varieties and yields abstract tilted Richardson varieties whose isomorphism classes, together with their labeled stratifications, are independent of the choices involved. We obtain an explicit formula for the point-counting polynomials of their open parts in terms of increasing minimal weight paths, extending Dyer's formula for Kazhdan--Lusztig $R$-polynomials. Over the real numbers, their totally nonnegative parts are regular CW complexes homeomorphic to closed balls, which gives a natural geometric realization of the posets of tilted Bruhat subintervals in all Lie types. Over the complex numbers, we prove that their fundamental classes push forward under a continuous loop evaluation map to the Poincar\'e duals of the minimal-degree coefficients of quantum Schubert products.
item.dc:creator: Xuhua He, Qingchao Yu

item.title: Cohen-Macaulay truncated path and Nakayama algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.15386v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper characterizes Cohen-Macaulay algebras in the sense of Auslander and Reiten [Progr. Math. 95(1991)] within the following two classes of finite dimensional algebras: (i) truncated path algebras and (ii) Nakayama algebras. For the former, our characterization in terms of ordinary quivers shows that if a Cohen-Macaulay truncated path algebra $\Lambda$ is connected, then $\Lambda$ or $D(\Lambda)$ gives a dualizing module, where $D$ denotes the standard duality. For the latter, we show that every Cohen-Macaulay Nakayama algebra $\Lambda$ is Iwanaga-Gorenstein. In particular, $\Lambda$ always gives a dualizing module. Consequently, there is no non-trivial Cohen-Macaulay algebra among truncated path and Nakayama algebras.
item.dc:creator: Takahiro Honma, Satoshi Usui

item.title: Total Cohomology of Hilbert schemes of Orbisurfaces I: Reduction to Stacky Loci
item.description: arXiv:2610.15688v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We generalize Nakajima's theory of Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces to Hilbert schemes of points on \textit{orbisurfaces}, and obtain initial factorization based on stratification by stabilizers. While the usual formula is retained for the trivial stabilizer stratum and for those strata of codimension $1$, genuine difficulties arise with stacky points strata. In the local picture of an isolated stacky point, the theory reduce to the study of $\Quot^\bfv[\CC^2/G]$ for a \textit{small} finite subgroup of $GL_2(\CC)$. The generating series for their total cohomology is a geometric correction of the generating series for total cohomology of ordinary smooth surface schemes. In addition, we obtain an action of the Borel-Moore homology of the punctual fibre stacks on the total Hilbert cohomology by virtual correspondences, in analogy with the Fock space description in Nakajima's theory. The punctual fibre stacks are genuinely different from the symmetric stack, and has natural realizations via motivic integration.
item.dc:creator: Shuo Gao

item.title: Spectra and Support Theory for Wide Subcategories in $n$-Abelian Categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.16541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a support theory for wide subcategories of essentially small Krull--Schmidt \(n\)-abelian categories. We construct spectra associated with families of wide subcategories and establish the corresponding support and radical theories. In particular, we characterize prime wide subcategories as the completely meet-irreducible elements of the lattice of wide subcategories and prove that every wide subcategory is recovered from the prime wide subcategories containing it. We further show that any classifying support datum is recovered, together with its object supports, from the canonical prime spectrum. Finally, we provide a \(2\)-abelian example admitting no classifying support datum.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Xin

item.title: The Quantum Character Transform
item.description: arXiv:2610.16827v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bastidas et al. (2025) highlighted the importance of exploiting group symmetries to reduce computational overhead and unify simulation methods across both condensed matter physics and ab initio quantum chemistry. I discuss the discrete character transform, which is the group Fourier transform restricted to $Z(\mathbb{C}[G])$, the center of the group algebra, where class functions form a commutative convolution algebra and irreducible characters are its spectral basis. The normalized character table of a non-abelian group can be obtained through a restriction operator, which means an efficient quantum character transform for any finite group with an efficient quantum Fourier transform. I give complementary quantum algorithms for class convolution based on direct class-sum block encoding and spectral implementation in the character basis, explaining their applications to symmetry-adapted many-body dynamics, molecular and spectroscopic symmetry analysis, and quantum walks, as well as characterizing the central information used in hidden-subgroup problems, including its limitations for graph isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Kagwe A. Muchane

item.title: A Gordon--Green-type result for Gorenstein-projective modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.17357v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let \(\Lambda\) be a \(\Z\)-graded Artin algebra which is Iwanaga--Gorenstein. We prove that \(\Lambda\) is CM-finite if and only if the category of gradable Gorenstein-projective modules has finite type, and if and only if the lengths of the indecomposable gradable Gorenstein-projective modules are bounded. Moreover, if \(\Lambda\) is CM-finite, then every Gorenstein-projective \(\Lambda\)-module is gradable. These results provide Gorenstein-projective analogues of the corresponding theorems of Gordon--Green for graded Artin algebras of finite representation type.
item.dc:creator: A. M. Bouhada, M. Laaraj

item.title: Linear Laurent phenomenon algebras are of finite type
item.description: arXiv:2610.17441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Laurent phenomenon algebras generalise cluster algebras by allowing irreducible exchange polynomials in place of binomials. Lam and Pylyavskyy proved finite type for those arising from graphs and conjectured that the same holds for every Laurent phenomenon algebra admitting a linear seed. We prove this conjecture over an arbitrary unique factorisation domain. Our proof constructs a nonzero element of the upper algebra divisible by every cluster variable. Comparing noninitial cluster variables with the prime factors of this element in the initial Laurent ring bounds the number of cluster variable classes and yields a finite normalised mutation pattern.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Daisey

item.title: On quasi-lisse affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories
item.description: arXiv:2610.17676v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study certain simple affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is a non-simply-laced simple Lie algebra and $h$ is its Coxeter number. For $L_{-3}(F_4)$, we determine the maximal ideal of $V^{-3}(F_4)$, Zhu's algebra, and the associated variety. We also classify the irreducible highest-weight $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules and determine the characters of its irreducible ordinary modules. The associated variety is $\overline{\mathbb{O}}_{\widetilde A_1}$, and the level $-3$ is totally collapsing for the orbit $\mathbb{O}_{\widetilde A_1}$. The Poisson coinvariants of the $C_2$-algebra of $L_{-3}(F_4)$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}[\ell]/(\ell^5)$, where $\ell$ is induced by the conformal vector. Consequently, the characters of ordinary $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules satisfy a fifth-order modular linear differential equation. We also give modular linear differential equations of orders five and eleven satisfied by the characters of ordinary modules for $L_{-2}(B_3)$ and $L_{-2}(G_2)$ respectively.
item.dc:creator: Drazen Adamovic, Xuanzhong Dai, Kaiwen Sun

item.title: Dimensions and maximal-dimensional components of higher commuting varieties of symmetric pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.17737v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathfrak p$ be the $(-1)$-eigenspace of a complex semisimple symmetric pair. For every $r\ge2$, we prove $\dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))\le \lfloor r\dim\mathfrak p/2\rfloor$ and show that every irreducible component is isotropic for a natural family of alternating forms. For a nonzero Hermitian pair with $\mathfrak g$ simple and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p^-\oplus\mathfrak p^+$, put $d=\dim\mathfrak p^+$ and $\ell=\operatorname{rk}(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak k)$. Then \[ \dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))=rd,\qquad \dim C_r(\mathfrak p)=\max\{rd,\,2d+(r-1)\ell\}. \] In this case we also determine the maximal-dimensional components of $C_r(\mathfrak p)$; for $r\ge3$, the only maximal-dimensional nilpotent components are $(\mathfrak p^+)^r$ and $(\mathfrak p^-)^r$. For arbitrary symmetric pairs, $\dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))=ra+m$ for all large $r$, where $a$ is the largest dimension of an abelian subspace of $\mathfrak p$ consisting of nilpotent elements and $m$ is the dimension of the variety of such subspaces. Applications give dimension and component formulas for equivariant punctual Quot schemes under explicit framing conditions, and bounds for punctual Gorenstein loci refined by socle parity.
item.dc:creator: Santosha Pattanayak

item.title: Quandles with isomorphic representation categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.17769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give two types of examples where two non isomorphic finite quandles have isomorphic enveloping groups. This implies that two non-isomorphic finite quandles can share isomorphic representation categories (as additive and tensor categories simultaneously).
item.dc:creator: Mohamad Maassarani

item.title: Beyond the circle: current algebras, geometry and higher gauge structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.17781v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Replacing the circle by a manifold leads to current Lie algebras and their central and derivation extensions. We separate the coefficient algebra, harmonic analysis and geometric data. Differentials modulo exact forms describe central extensions; divergence-free vector fields give explicit cocycles, whose compatible derivations satisfy a stabilizer equation. Compact examples include the three-sphere and its current--Virasoro extension. We also explain the analytic qualifications for SL(2,R) and its symmetric space and the role of transported multiplication in soft geometries. The recent harmonic constructions of Campoamor-Stursberg, Marrani and Rausch de Traubenberg are compared with the cohomological work of Coquereaux, Frappat, Ragoucy and Sorba and Castellani's loop geometry and infinite-dimensional free differential algebras. A coefficient-algebra construction connects currents to higher brackets and clarifies the additional requirements of a dynamical theory. For Lie algebras of order F, central extensions obey coupled binary and symmetric F-ary conditions, with explicit examples and obstructions.
item.dc:creator: R. Campoamor-Stursberg, A. Marrani, M. Rausch de Traubenberg

item.title: The equivariant Ehrhart theory of polytopes with order-two symmetries: Part II
item.description: arXiv:2610.17988v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give two counterexamples to Stapledon's Effectiveness Conjecture. Each counterexample is a $6$-dimensional lattice polytope with an order-two symmetry whose equivariant $H^*$-series $\varphi[t]$ is a polynomial with one coefficient that is not effective. For polytopes with a symmetry of order two, the goal of this paper is to build up a picture of the landscape of results for when the Effectiveness Conjecture holds. Our main result is a criterion, in terms of the faces of $P$, that determines when the Ehrhart ring of $P$ admits an invariant linear system of parameters of the correct representation type. We use these results to reduce the space of possible counterexamples to one of two cases. A randomised computer search produced counterexamples in each case. We also give an example where the equivariant $H^*$-series is effective but admits no invariant linear system of parameters, neither for $P$ nor any invariant subdivision of it, answering a question of Stapledon in the case of groups of order two.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Clarke

item.title: River ribbon tableaux and symmetric group characters
item.description: arXiv:2610.18239v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce river ribbon tableaux, where a river of non-trivial ribbons is placed between two banks of single boxes. Compared to other ribbon peelings, this reduces the geometric differences across diagrams of different shapes, and the maximal number of ribbon configurations. This allows us to prove a uniform character bound for symmetric groups which, specialized to balanced diagrams, proves the conjecture of Moore and Russell. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Dousse and F\'eray on the number of standard tableaux of skew shapes.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Teyssier

item.title: Okubo algebras and Exceptional Periodicity: tetracode gradings, root-lattice obstructions and Clifford cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.18643v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Okubo algebra brings together ternary gradings, integral root frames and rank-three geometry. We examine how these structures extend to the complex Exceptional Periodicity algebras. With $N=4(n+1)$, a tetracode character gives eight nonzero homogeneous components of dimension $t_n=8n+3+2^{4n}$. On a tip, a compatible grading has zero component of dimension $8n-5$ and eight nonzero components of dimension $1+2^{4n-3}$. The arithmetic behaves differently: for $n\geq2$, the lattice $D_N^+$ has no full-rank orthogonal frame of unscaled $A_2$ lattices. We exhibit failures of the Jacobi and Jordan identities and determine the derivations and full automorphism group of the ambient algebra above level one. We also give a Clifford-module proof, with the normalization fixed by root products, of the published realization of EP tips as special Vinberg $H$-algebras. This identifies a positive real form and yields explicit formulas for its cone, cubic, Cholesky coordinates and rational dual invariant. The cone is symmetric exactly at $n=1$. Its determinant-one hypersurface belongs to the known $L(8n,1,0)$ series, whose $r$- and $c$-maps give homogeneous scalar manifolds for supergravity theories with eight real supercharges.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Marrani, Daniele Corradetti

item.title: Cellular Algebra of $A_2$ webs
item.description: arXiv:2610.18801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a diagram algebra $\mathcal{K}_L$ based on Kuperberg's $A_2$-webs and prove a Schur--Weyl duality $\mathcal{K}_L \cong \operatorname{End}_{U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)}((V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L})$, where $V^\pm$ are the fundamental representations of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$. Thus, $\mathcal{K}_L$ is a natural $A_2$ analogue of the Temperley--Lieb algebra. We construct an explicit cellular structure for $\mathcal{K}_L$, with the web basis as its cellular basis and cell modules indexed by dominant $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$-weights. The bases of these modules are parametrized by dominant lattice paths via a recursive growth algorithm. Using this structure, we determine local generators of $\mathcal{K}_L$ and establish web formulations of the first and second fundamental theorems of invariant theory. In particular, we show that the braid-group image, augmented by local idempotents, does not generate $\mathcal{K}_L$, and identify an additional local generator. Finally, we derive a bimodule decomposition of $(V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L}$, yielding a complete set of irreducible $\mathcal{K}_L$-modules for formal or generic $q$.
item.dc:creator: Azat M. Gainutdinov, Jesper Lykke Jacobsen, Yueheng Li

item.title: Counting irreducible representations of general linear groups and unitary groups
item.description: arXiv:2504.11403v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a general linear group over $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, or $\mathbb{H}$, or a real unitary group. In this paper, we precisely describe the number of isomorphism classes of irreducible Casselman-Wallach representations of $G$ with a given infinitesimal character and a given associated variety, expressed in terms of certain combinatorial data called painted Young diagrams and assigned Young diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Qiutong Wang

item.title: Stranding $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ webs
item.description: arXiv:2510.12035v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Webs are planar directed graphs that encode invariant vectors for tensor products of fundamental $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-representations. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, web calculus is governed by effective reduction rules and well-understood reduced-web bases, but these features break down in higher rank. In this paper we develop a global combinatorial framework for untagged $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ webs, called \emph{strandings}, which organizes local labeling data into systems of colored directed paths on the web graph. Our main result is an explicit state-sum formula for the invariant vector of an untagged web as a weighted sum over its valid strandings. The usual labeling-based construction requires a choice of decomposition into elementary web pieces and a vertex-by-vertex coefficient calculation. Our global reformulation avoids both. We prove that the vectors produced by strandings are $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-invariant, compare the untagged theory with the tagged-web framework of Cautis, Kamnitzer, and Morrison, and use this comparison to obtain a complete set of relations for untagged web graphs. We also give applications of strandings to nonvanishing results, basis constructions from tableaux, and connections with Springer-theoretic combinatorics.
item.dc:creator: Heather M. Russell, Julianna Tymoczko

item.title: On the computation of the canonical basis for irreducible highest weight $U_q (\mathfrak{gl}_{\infty})$-modules
item.description: arXiv:2601.16889v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study canonical basis elements in higher-level Fock spaces associated with the quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{gl}_\infty)$, which are conjecturally related to Calogero-Moser theory for complex reflection groups. We generalize the Leclerc-Miyachi formula to arbitrary levels by introducing new explicit constructions based on symbols, including a column removal theorem and closed formulas in several cases. These results provide explicit descriptions of canonical basis elements with applications to Calogero-Moser cellular characters and to the decomposition matrices of Ariki-Koike algebras.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Jacon, Abel Lacabanne

item.title: Pseudo-torsion classes
item.description: arXiv:2603.27709v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a finite dimensional algebra $\Lambda$, we consider a torsion class $G$ in $mod$-$\Lambda$, which is not necessarily functorially finite. We construct a wall-and-chamber structure for $G$ where the chambers are the connected components of the complement of the union of walls. We call these ``pseudo-chambers''. We also consider ``infinitesimal chambers". To each pseudo-chamber $U$ we associate a ``pseudo-torsion class'' $P(U)$ and a ``pseudo-torsionfree class'' $Q(U)$ and show that they determine $U$. Furthermore, we show that if both $P(U)$ and $Q(U)$ are finitely generated, then $U$ is an open set. We consider ``green paths'' in the stability space and associate to them Harder-Narasimhan stratifications of $G$. This paper is part of a series of papers whose goal is to study the ``ghosts'' which are remnants of the indecomposable $\Lambda$-modules which do not lie in $G$. In the special case when our torsion class is all of $mod$-$\Lambda$, we are in the classical well-known setting. All of our results apply to this classical setting. The ``pseudo-torsion classes'' are torsion classes. We point out that we do not take the closure of the set of walls. So, we get more pseudo-chambers and our results are new even in this classical setting.
item.dc:creator: Kiyoshi Igusa, Ray Maresca

item.title: Pointwise character bounds for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$
item.description: arXiv:2604.17589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a basic pointwise bound for the irreducible characters of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ and, as an application, derive new $L^p$ bounds for these characters. Our approach is based on the descent of characters to singular sets and the cancellation in this formula.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 58 (2026), no. 10, Paper No. e70519, 24 pp
item.dc:creator: Yunfeng Zhang

item.title: Middle convolution for Lie algebra representations
item.description: arXiv:2605.09828v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper introduces a Lie algebra analogue of the middle convolution functor, which is defined on the category of modules over certain Lie algebras, including, as typical motivating examples, free Lie algebras, Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras, and the holonomy Lie algebras of complements of hyperplane arrangements. First, we demonstrate that the middle convolution for Lie algebra representations can be regarded as a natural generalization of the infinitesimal analogue of the Long-Moody functor for Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras. Second, we show that our middle convolution recovers the Dettweiler-Reiter additive middle convolution for Fuchsian systems on the punctured Riemann sphere as a special case. Furthermore, we show that when applied to the holonomy Lie algebra of the complement of a hyperplane arrangement, our functor is compatible with Haraoka's middle convolution for logarithmic connections on such complements. Finally, we establish a Riemann-Hilbert correspondence between the middle convolution for the holonomy Lie algebra and the middle convolution for local systems on complements of hyperplane arrangements.
item.dc:creator: Kazuki Hiroe

item.title: Gelfand--Kirillov dimensions of highest weight modules for basic classical Lie superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2606.11551v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give exact Gelfand--Kirillov (GK) dimension formulas for simple highest weight modules of the basic classical Lie superalgebras considered in this paper. For the type II orthosymplectic algebras $D(m,n)$ and $B(m,n)$, we identify the PBW associated variety as a product of factor supports evaluated at highest weights for two compatible Borel subalgebras. This gives algorithms for arbitrary complex highest weights, without integrality or typicality hypotheses. In type $B$, the terminal factor is $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$, for which we derive an insertion formula that distinguishes integer and half-integer shifted coordinates. For $G(3)$, $F(4)$ and $D(2,1;\alpha)$, finite odd-reflection procedures give exact formulas, their GK spectra, and finite-dimensionality criteria; we also describe the dependence on $\alpha$ in the last case. In type I, the GK dimension equals that of the simple even highest weight module for the distinguished Borel. The computations use the established ordinary Lie algebra formulas involving Lusztig's $\mathbf a$-function and Robinson--Schensted insertion.
item.dc:creator: Jing Jiang

item.title: Total positivity and symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2606.25516v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define a notion of total positivity for the symmetric space $G/K$ by taking the Hausdorff closure of the image of Lusztig's totally positive part $G_{>0}$ in $G/K$. We introduce double Bruhat cells for the symmetric space and define their totally positive pieces. We prove a cell decomposition of the totally nonnegative symmetric space, give explicit positive parametrizations of all cells, establish closure relations, and show that the transition maps between the two natural families of parametrizations are subtraction-free.
item.dc:creator: Huanchen Bao

item.title: Hopf $2$-cocycles for certain affine algebraic reductive groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.18599v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a reductive affine algebraic group over $\mathbb C$ with toral identity component $T$ and finite component group $K$. We describe finite indecomposable semisimple module categories over $\Rep(G)$ using equivariant data that incorporate the extension class. We prove that every fiber functor is classical and determine the image of its Hopf $2$-cocycle support in $K$ and its intersection with $T$. This yields a minimality criterion involving a finite stabilizer cocycle and an alternating bicharacter on a sublattice of $\widehat T$ of index at most $|K|$. When $\dim T=1$, every Hopf $2$-cocycle for $G$ has finite support of order at most $|K|^2$. We compute all gauge classes for the split and nonsplit extensions with component group $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ and inversion action, and compare the support formulas with the K\"unneth coordinates for commutative direct products. Finally, for an arbitrary reductive group $G$, a minimal Hopf $2$-cocycle in a regular deformation of the trivial Hopf $2$-cocycle forces $G$ to be a torus. This uses locality and rigidity of algebraic matrix coefficients on the semisimple quotient of $G$.
item.dc:creator: Shlomo Gelaki

item.title: On the natural transformations of extension functors
item.description: arXiv:2607.23495v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Assume that $n$ is a non-negative integer and $\C$ an $n$-Frobenius category. This paper is concerned with the natural transformations between extension functors on $\C$. The main result of the paper indicates that for any pair of objects $M, N\in \C$, the group of all natural transformations from $\Ext^{n+1}_{\C}(N, -)$ to $\Ext^{n+1}_{\C}(M, -)$ is isomorphic to the quotient group $\Ext^n_{\C}(M, \syz^nN)/{\p}$, where $\p$ is the subgroup consisting of those Yoneda extensions of length $n$ arising as a push-out along a morphism $P\rt\syz^nN$, with $P$ $n$-projective. This result is fruitful from the point of view that, $n$-Frobenius categories may not have projective objects.
item.dc:creator: Abdolnaser Bahlekeh, Shokrollah Salarian

item.title: Moduli of super-representations of quivers
item.description: arXiv:2608.13375v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note, we construct moduli spaces of super-representations of quivers by extending King's Geometric Invariant Theory (GIT) framework to the super setting. Using the even part of super general linear groups and a parity-shifting operator, we construct moduli spaces that topologically parameterize super-representations of a fixed super-dimension. We also outline the construction of super quiver varieties for super-representations of framed quivers (without doubling); and realise super-Grassmannians and super-flag varieties as geometric quotients within this setting.
item.dc:creator: Sanjay Amrutiya, Umesh Dubey

item.title: Recollements of derived categories from $n$-term big tilting complexes
item.description: arXiv:2608.19921v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $A$ be a ring, let ${\bf T}$ be a finite-term big tilting complex over $A$, and choose a bounded projective representative $\cpx{P}$ of ${\bf T}$. Put $B=\End_{\D{A}}(\cpx{P})$. We prove that the kernel of the associated derived tensor functor ${\bf R}:\D{B}\to\D{A}$ is equivalent, through the derived inclusion, to $\D{\mathscr E}$, where $\mathscr E=\Ker({\bf R})\cap B\Modcat$ carries the inherited exact structure. Consequently, $\D{B}$ admits a recollement by $\D{\mathscr E}$ and $\D{A}$. The proof combines a dg double-centralizer argument with a functorial realisation of the kernel on unbounded complexes. The category $\mathscr E$ is definable and $d$-symmetric whenever $d$ is at least the projective amplitude of the underlying perfect right $B$-complex. We also characterise when the kernel is induced by a homological ring epimorphism: this holds precisely when $\mathscr E$ is an abelian subcategory, or equivalently when the standard $t$-structure restricts to the kernel. In amplitude at most one, this recovers the universal-localisation description for two-term big tilting complexes. Over semiperfect endomorphism rings, the amplitude is detected by reduction modulo the Jacobson radical. Finally, we construct non-compact examples of arbitrarily large minimal projective amplitude. One family yields algebraic Calkin quotients; another, over connected rings constructed from singular local hypersurfaces, has nonzero, non-abelian exact kernels and cannot be obtained from modules by derived equivalences between ordinary rings.
item.dc:creator: Shengyong Pan, Huabo Xu

item.title: Polynomiality for algebras of invariants associated with some In\"on\"u-Wigner contractions in type A
item.description: arXiv:2609.01173v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper deals with polynomiality of algebras of symmetric invariants (or generated by symmetric semi-invariants) associated with some particular In\"on\"u-Wigner contractions in type A. More precisely we are interested with contractions of some parabolic subalgebras in type A with respect to their decomposition into their Levi factor and their nilpotent radical, the latter becoming an abelian ideal of the contraction. When the parabolic subalgebra $\mathfrak p$ has its Levi factor decomposing into three blocks, which are symmetric with respect to the antidiagonal, we show in this article that the algebra of symmetric invariants associated with the contraction of the canonical truncation of $\mathfrak p$ has a Weistrass section. It follows that such an algebra of invariants is a polynomial algebra, for which we can give the number of algebraically independent homogeneous generators, their weight and degree. The method relies on the construction of an adapted pair for such a contraction. When the Levi factor of $\mathfrak p$ has its central block not of the same size as its two extremal blocks, we also show that the above algebra of symmetric invariants is equal to the algebra generated by symmetric semi-invariants associated with the In\"on\"u-Wigner contraction of $\mathfrak p$.
item.dc:creator: Florence Fauquant-Millet

item.title: Differential calculus on quantized irreducible flag manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.13687v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a new description of the differential calculus on the quantized irreducible flag manifold given by Heckenberger-Kolb. We also define a quantum analogue of the Dolbeault complex associated to an equivariant vector bundle on the irreducible flag manifold, and show that its cohomology groups coincide with the cohomology groups given by Andersen-Polo-Wen defined using the induction functor.
item.dc:creator: Toshiyuki Tanisaki

item.title: Rotation fixed points of undecorated braid varieties and fusion rings of affine Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.02034v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a simply connected semisimple algebraic group. On the (undecorated) braid variety associated with a power of a Coxeter element, there is a finite-order autoequivalence, called the Zamolodchikov transformation, induced by cyclic rotation of words. In this paper, we show that the coarse moduli space of the fixed-point stack of this autoequivalence is isomorphic to the spectrum of the fusion ring of the corresponding affine Lie algebra. The above results also extend to twisted Coxeter elements, and the fusion rings of all affine Lie algebras are obtained in this way.
item.dc:creator: Yuma Mizuno

item.title: Combinatorics of Mirkovi\'c-Vilonen cycles in twisted affine Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2610.04730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the explicit geometric and combinatorial structure of Mirkovi\'c-Vilonen (MV) cycles in twisted affine Grassmannians associated with special parahoric group schemes. Using the twist map on configuration spaces of decorated flags, we obtain an explicit parametrization of twisted MV cycles by Lusztig data. We show that the changes between reduced words are governed by the usual Lusztig transformations for the reductive group arising from ramified geometric Satake correspondence. As a consequence, the moment polytopes of twisted MV cycles coincide with the usual MV polytopes for this group. Our construction applies to all special parahoric subgroups in the tamely ramified setting.
item.dc:creator: Jiuzu Hong, Linhui Shen, Daping Weng

item.title: Ramified Quivers with Potentials, Monodromy Characters, and Cluster Bases I
item.description: arXiv:2610.09868v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct categorical models and cluster characters for skew-symmetrizable cluster algebras admitting good ramified realizations. Goodness is equivalent to nondegenerate realizability. When a reddening sequence is given, it is enough to check sign coherence of the arrow types along that sequence. Triangular extensions with arbitrary connecting bimodule types preserve goodness when both component matrices admit reddening sequences. Consequently, every matrix obtained from one vertex by triangular extensions and mutations admits a good Jacobi-finite nondegenerate realization for every compatible positive integral symmetrizer. For a good Jacobi-finite nondegenerate realization, the monodromy $F$-polynomials satisfy mutation for all finite decorated representations, without a rigidity hypothesis. A full initial order determines valued universal presentations and their cluster characters. Under the reachability condition, these characters form a basis of the middle cluster algebra for arbitrary geometric coefficients, with frozen variables inverted, and contain all cluster monomials. The same family is an upper-cluster-algebra basis when the middle and upper algebras coincide. For a fixed Jacobian algebra and $\delta$-vector, the Newton polytope of the generic monodromy $F$-polynomial is independent of the order.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: Categorified Cluster Structures on Coulomb Branches of Certain Star-Shaped Quivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.11427v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the quantized $K$-theoretic Coulomb branches of framed star-shaped quivers with central gauge dimension $n\geq2$, $r-1$ one-dimensional outer gauge vertices, and a one-dimensional framing at the central vertex. For $n=2$ and arbitrary $r\geq1$, and for every $n\geq2$ with $1\leq r\leq5$, we prove that the loop-graded Koszul-perverse heart is a monoidal categorification of the associated quantum cluster algebra over $\mathbb{Z}[v^{\pm1}]$. This quantum cluster algebra coincides with its upper quantum cluster algebra. For all $n\geq2$ and $r\geq1$, we construct an explicit initial seed and identify the associated upper quantum cluster algebra with the Grothendieck ring of this heart. Every mutation is realized by a short exact sequence, and every quantum cluster monomial is represented by a simple object.
item.dc:creator: Tianle Liu

item.title: Sharp commutator bounds on complex simple Lie algebras: the B\"ottcher--Wenzel inequality and the comass of the Cartan $3$-form
item.description: arXiv:2610.11800v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a complex simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ with compact conjugation $\tau$, Killing form $B$, and Hermitian form $H(x, y) = -B(x, \tau y)$, it is shown that $H([x,y],[x,y]) \leq (h^{\vee})^{-1}H(x,x)H(y,y)$, where $h^{\vee}$ is the dual Coxeter number, with equality exactly for $H$-orthogonal pairs in $\tau$-stable long-root subalgebras isomorphic to $\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{C})$. Equivalently, the comass of the Cartan $3$-form with respect to $H$ equals its comass on the compact real form: the spectral norm of the Cartan $3$-form does not increase under complexification. For the Frobenius norm on the image of a representation of Dynkin index $\ell$ the optimal constant is $2/\ell$; this contains the B\"ottcher--Wenzel and Bloch--Iserles inequalities, extends the latter to complex skew-symmetric matrices, and improves them substantially for the exceptional Lie algebras of types $F_{4}$, $E_{6}$, $E_{7}$, and $E_{8}$. The proof uses the Nahm algebra of $\mathfrak{g}$ with the conjugation induced by $\tau$: critical points of the relevant function correspond to $\tau$-twisted idempotents, and its Hessian is governed by $\tau$-twisted multiplication operators, whose anticommutation with multiplication by $i$ turns the one-sided second order condition at a maximum into a two-sided spectral bound. Subalgebras isomorphic to $\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{C})$ of Dynkin index $j$ give critical points with critical value $1/(jh^{\vee})$, whose Morse indices are computed, and the set of maximum points is a nondegenerate critical manifold. Geometrically, the maximal complex sectional curvature of a compact simple Lie group equals its maximal sectional curvature.
item.dc:creator: Daniel J. F. Fox

item.title: Cell decomposition and dual boundary complexes of character varieties
item.description: arXiv:2307.16657v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The weak geometric P=W conjecture of Katzarkov--Noll--Pandit--Simpson asserts that for any smooth Betti moduli space $\mathcal{M}_B$ of complex dimension $d$ associated to a punctured Riemann surface, the dual boundary complex $\mathbb{D}\partial\mathcal{M}_B$ is homotopy equivalent to a $(d-1)$-sphere. Here, $\mathcal{M}_B$ is a generic $GL_n(\mathbb{C})$-character variety of genus $g$, with prescribed semisimple local monodromies at $k$ punctures. In this article, we prove the weak geometric P=W conjecture for all \emph{very generic} $\mathcal{M}_B$, namely when at least one conjugacy class is regular semisimple. A key step is a strengthening of Mellit's cell decomposition theorem: we decompose $\mathcal{M}_B$ itself (without passing to a vector bundle) into locally closed subvarieties which are stably isomorphic to $(\mathbb{C}^{\times})^{d-2b}\times \mathbb{C}^b$. A second ingredient is a motivic characterization of the integral cohomology of dual boundary complexes, developed in [Su24]. Following Simpson's strategy, the proof reduces to an inductive computation of dual boundary complexes arising from this cell decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Tao Su

item.title: Injectivity and stability for the sub-Riemannian X-ray transform on H-type groups
item.description: arXiv:2312.00594v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove injectivity and a stability estimate for the X-ray transform along sub-Riemannian geodesics of $H$-type groups, a setting in which almost every geodesic carries conjugate points. The geodesics are helices labeled by a charge $\lambda$ valued in the dual of the center. We prove a Fourier slice theorem, which identifies the X-ray transform over geodesics with charge $\lambda$ as the restriction of the group Fourier transform to their visible frequencies, followed by an explicit multiplier. We characterize the sets of charges whose geodesics determine an integrable function, as exactly those whose visible frequencies are dense. In particular, when the center of the group has dimension at least two, charges of a single magnitude suffice provided their directions fill a great circle. Laguerre asymptotics on the spectrum of the normal operator at fixed charge yields a stability estimate at every nonzero visible frequency with the loss of exactly half a derivative in the sub-Laplacian, except on the first Heisenberg group. Finally, we prove that data limited to a band or a cap of charges determines all sufficiently high central frequencies of an unknown function.
item.dc:creator: Steven Flynn

item.title: Level one automorphic representations of an anisotropic exceptional group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$
item.description: arXiv:2407.05859v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Up to isomorphism, there is a unique connected semisimple algebraic group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of Lie type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$, with compact real points and split over $\mathbb{Q}_{p}$ for all primes $p$. Let $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ be such a group. In this paper, we study the level one automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ in the spirit of the work of Chenevier, Renard, and Ta\"ibi. First, we give an explicit formula for the number of these representations having any given archimedean component. For this, we study the automorphism group of the two definite exceptional Jordan algebras of rank $27$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ studied by Gross, as well as the dimension of the invariants of these groups in all irreducible representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}(\mathbb{R})$. Then, assuming standard conjectures by Arthur and Langlands for $\mathbf{F}_{4}$, we refine this counting by studying the contribution of the representations whose global Arthur parameter has any possible image (or "Sato-Tate group"). This includes a detailed description of all those images, as well as precise statements for the Arthur's multiplicity formula in each case. As a consequence, we obtain a conjectural but explicit formula for the number of algebraic, cuspidal, level one automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_{26}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with Sato-Tate group $\mathbf{F}_{4}(\mathbb{R})$ of any given weight (assumed "$\mathrm{F}_{4}$-regular"). The first example of such representations occurs in motivic weight $36$.
item.dc:creator: Yi Shan

item.title: Root data in character varieties
item.description: arXiv:2408.03111v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given $G$ an algebraic reductive group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and $\Gamma$ a finitely generated group, we provide a stratification of the $G$-character variety of $\Gamma$ in terms of conjugacy classes of parabolic subgroups of $G$. Each stratum has the structure of a pseudo-quotient, which is a relaxed GIT notion capturing the topology of the quotient and, therefore, behaving well for motivic computations of invariants of the character varieties. These stratifications are constructed by analyzing the root datum of $G$ to encode parabolic classes. Finally, detailed and explicit motivic formulae are provided for cases with Dynkin diagram of types $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$.
item.dc:creator: \'Angel Gonz\'alez-Prieto, Alfonso Zamora

item.title: The global exceptional theta correspondence for the dual pair $\mathbf{F}_{4}\times \mathbf{PGL}_{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2501.19101v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ be the unique (up to isomorphism) connected semisimple algebraic group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$, with compact real points and split over $\mathbb{Q}_{p}$ for all primes $p$. A conjectural computation by the author in arxiv:2407.05859 predicts the existence of a family of level one automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$, which are expected to be functorial lifts of cuspidal representations of $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$ associated with Hecke eigenforms. In this paper, we study the exceptional theta correspondence for $\mathbf{F}_{4}\times\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$, and establish the existence of such a family of automorphic representations for $\mathbf{F}_{4}$. Moreover, we show that for the automorphic form on $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$ associated with any even weight $k\geq 12$, level $N$ cuspidal eigenform, its global theta lift to $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ is non-zero. For the other direction, motivated by the work of Pollack, we develop a notion of "exceptional theta series" on $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$, arising from certain automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$. These theta series are holomorphic modular forms on $\mathbf{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})$, with explicit Fourier expansions, and span the entire space of level one cusp forms.
item.dc:creator: Yi Shan

item.title: Shift orbifolds, decompactification limits, and lattices
item.description: arXiv:2502.18453v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe the general shift orbifold of a Narain CFT and use this to investigate decompactification limits in the heterotic Narain moduli space. We also comment on higher rank theories and describe some applications to the CFT based on the Leech lattice and its shift orbifolds.
